Le backlog est à jour (`docs/backlog.md`, rien de nouveau depuis le rename du module en #4). J'ai vérifié la couverture réelle — elle correspond aux chiffres du doc.

## La suite immédiate : finir la phase 1 de la couverture

C'est la seule ligne du backlog explicitement « en cours ». Restent trois packages (~255 statements) :

| Package | Actuel | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/gitlab` | **7.5 %** | le plus gros gain ; client API, à tester via `httptest` |
| `internal/credentials` | **29.5 %** | `FileStorage` / `MemoryStorage` testables directement, `GitCredentialStorage` demande un seam d'exec |
| `internal/ui/theme` | **78.9 %** | complément (helpers `Bg`/`PadWithBg`/`TimeAgo`, `TableStylesFor*`) |

Un package n'apparaît dans aucune phase du plan : **`internal/registrymgr` à 18.5 %**. Oubli à corriger dans le tableau.

## Ensuite, un arbitrage à trancher avant la phase 2

Le backlog le signale mais ne le résout pas : les vues de la phase 2/3 (`security/model.go` 1785 lignes, `oci_resources/update.go` 1556, `app.go` 1333…) dépassent le plafond de 800 lignes. Écrire quelques milliers de statements de tests contre elles **fige leur structure actuelle**. Deux ordres possibles :

1. **Découper d'abord** — plus lent à démarrer, mais les tests écrits ensuite restent valides.
2. **Tester d'abord** — filet de sécurité pour le découpage, mais tests à réécrire après.

Mon avis : découper d'abord `internal/docker/client.go`, parce qu'il est de toute façon bloquant — la phase 5 ne peut pas commencer sans un seam d'exécution injectable (il `exec` le CLI Docker en direct). Ce refactor sert deux objectifs à la fois.

## Défauts : les moins chers d'abord

**D1** (`ReportModal` tronque sur les octets → UTF-8 invalide) et **D6** (`wordWrap` mesure des octets) sont la même classe de bug, tous deux épinglés par des tests en `t.Skip()`, tous deux corrigeables en quelques lignes avec `runewidth`. **D3** (boucle infinie si `wrapWidth <= 0`) est un garde d'une ligne. Les trois tiennent dans une seule PR.

**D2** et **D4** demandent une décision de ta part, pas du code : D2 = soit verrouiller la checkbox, soit retirer l'affirmation du commentaire ; D4 = changer `Tab` en `↑/↓` casse la mémoire musculaire.

Par quoi je commence — la phase 1, le refactor `docker/client.go`, ou le lot de défauts UTF-8 ?

13	// PullReport contains the results of a recursive pull operation
14	type PullReport struct {
15		Cloned  []string
16		Skipped []string
17		Errors  []string
18	}
19	
20	// ReportModal displays the results of an operation
21	type ReportModal struct {
22		title        string
23		report       PullReport
24		scrollOffset int
25		maxVisible   int
26		activeTab    int // 0 = Cloned, 1 = Skipped, 2 = Errors
27		width        int
28		height       int
29	}
30	
31	// NewReportModal creates a new report modal
32	func NewReportModal(title string, report PullReport) *ReportModal {
33		return &ReportModal{
34			title:        title,
35			report:       report,
36			scrollOffset: 0,
37			maxVisible:   10,
38			activeTab:    0,
39		}
40	}
41	
42	// ReportModalCloseMsg is sent when the modal is closed
43	type ReportModalCloseMsg struct{}
44	
45	// Update handles messages
46	func (m *ReportModal) Update(msg tea.Msg) (*ReportModal, tea.Cmd) {
47		switch msg := msg.(type) {
48		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
49			m.width = msg.Width
50			m.height = msg.Height
51	
52		case tea.KeyMsg:
53			switch msg.String() {
54			case "tab", "right", "l":
55				// Switch tab
56				m.activeTab = (m.activeTab + 1) % 3
57				m.scrollOffset = 0
58	
59			case "shift+tab", "left", "h":
60				// Switch tab backwards
61				m.activeTab = (m.activeTab + 2) % 3
62				m.scrollOffset = 0
63	
64			case "up", "k":
65				if m.scrollOffset > 0 {
66					m.scrollOffset--
67				}
68	
69			case "down", "j":
70				currentList := m.getCurrentList()
71				if m.scrollOffset < len(currentList)-m.maxVisible {
72					m.scrollOffset++
73				}
74	
75			case "enter", "esc", "q":
76				return m, func() tea.Msg {
77					return ReportModalCloseMsg{}
78				}
79			}
80		}
81	
82		return m, nil
83	}
84	
85	// getCurrentList returns the currently active list
86	func (m *ReportModal) getCurrentList() []string {
87		switch m.activeTab {
88		case 0:
89			return m.report.Cloned
90		case 1:
91			return m.report.Skipped
92		case 2:
93			return m.report.Errors
94		default:
95			return []string{}
96		}
97	}
98	
99	// View renders the modal
100	func (m *ReportModal) View() string {
101		var b strings.Builder
102	
103		// Title
104		b.WriteString(theme.TitleStyle.Render(m.title))
105		b.WriteString("\n\n")
106	
107		// Summary
108		summary := fmt.Sprintf("✓ %d cloned  •  ⊘ %d skipped  •  ✗ %d errors",
109			len(m.report.Cloned),
110			len(m.report.Skipped),
111			len(m.report.Errors),
112		)
113		summaryStyle := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Bold(true)
114		b.WriteString(summaryStyle.Render(summary))
115		b.WriteString("\n\n")
116	
117		// Tabs
118		tabs := m.renderTabs()
119		b.WriteString(tabs)
120		b.WriteString("\n\n")
121	
122		// Current list content
123		currentList := m.getCurrentList()
124		if len(currentList) == 0 {
125			emptyMsg := theme.DimStyle.Render("(empty)")
126			b.WriteString(emptyMsg)
127		} else {
128			// Render visible items
129			endIdx := m.scrollOffset + m.maxVisible
130			if endIdx > len(currentList) {
131				endIdx = len(currentList)
132			}
133	
134			for i := m.scrollOffset; i < endIdx; i++ {
135				item := currentList[i]
136				// Truncate long paths
137				if len(item) > 55 {
138					item = "..." + item[len(item)-52:]
139				}
140				b.WriteString("  • " + item + "\n")
141			}
142	
143			// Scroll indicator
144			if len(currentList) > m.maxVisible {
145				scrollInfo := theme.DimStyle.Render(
146					fmt.Sprintf("  [%d-%d of %d] ↑↓ to scroll",
147						m.scrollOffset+1,
148						endIdx,
149						len(currentList)),
150				)
151				b.WriteString("\n" + scrollInfo)
152			}
153		}
154	
155		b.WriteString("\n\n")
156	
157		// Help
158		// help := theme.HelpStyle.Render("[tab/←→] switch tab  [↑↓] scroll  [enter/esc] close")
159		// b.WriteString(help)

161		return lipgloss.NewStyle().
162			Background(theme.ColorBackground).
163			Foreground(theme.ColorText).
164			Border(lipgloss.NormalBorder()).
165			BorderForeground(theme.ColorPrimary).
166			BorderBackground(theme.ColorBackground).
167			Padding(1, 2).

# DevDesk Backlog

**Last Updated:** 2026-08-01

Open work for DevDesk: known defects, technical debt, and planned features.
Replaces the former `todo.md` at the repository root. Items completed there
(network topology visualisation, inter-container ping/curl) have been dropped
rather than carried over.

---

## 1. Known defects

None of these are fixed. Each is reachable from the current code unless noted.

### D1 — `ReportModal.View()` emits invalid UTF-8

`internal/ui/components/report_modal.go:136-139`

Long entries are truncated with `item[len(item)-52:]`, which slices **bytes**, not
runes. When the resulting offset falls inside a multi-byte codepoint the rendered
output is no longer valid UTF-8 and the terminal shows replacement characters.

Reachable with any non-ASCII repository path. Pinned by
`TestReportModalViewTruncationSplitsMultibyteRunes`, which `t.Skip()`s with
instructions once the truncation becomes rune-aware.

**Fix:** truncate on `[]rune`, and measure width with `runewidth` rather than
`len()`.

### D2 — The "permanent delete" checkbox is documented as locked but is not

`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:35` and `:99-105`

`NewDeleteConfirmModalPermanent` pre-checks *Immediate deletion* and its doc
comment states the box is non-modifiable ("pré-cochée et non modifiable"). Nothing
enforces that: `space` and `enter` on the checkbox still toggle it.

A project already marked for deletion can therefore be sent through a
grace-period delete that the caller does not expect. Pinned by
`TestDeleteConfirmModalPermanentCheckboxIsStillToggleable`.

**Fix:** carry a `locked` flag on the modal and make the toggle a no-op when set,
or drop the claim from the doc comment.

### D3 — `wrapInputLines` loops forever when `wrapWidth <= 0`

`internal/ui/components/wrapped_input.go:135`

With a non-positive wrap width the loop makes no progress: `breakAt` collapses to
`start`, an empty line is appended, and `start` never advances — the line slice
grows until the process runs out of memory.

**Not reachable today.** Every caller passes 60, 80 or 100 per Rule 133. Latent
only, which is why no test covers it (the test would hang).

**Fix:** guard the entry point — return a single line when `wrapWidth < 1`.

### D4 — `DeleteConfirmModal` uses `Tab` for field navigation

`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:89-97`

`tab` / `shift+tab` cycle checkbox → Yes → No. Rule 135 reserves those keys for
tab switching and assigns field navigation to `↑ / ↓` exclusively.

Cosmetic in isolation, but it is the kind of inconsistency Rule 135 exists to
prevent. Changing it alters muscle memory, so it needs a deliberate call rather
than a drive-by fix.

### D5 — Unreachable focus clamp in `CreationForm`

`internal/ui/components/creation_form.go:221-223`

After cycling the resource type, the code clamps `focusedField` down to
`maxField()`. The surrounding branch only runs when `focusedField == 0`, and
`maxField()` is never below 4, so the clamp can never fire.

Dead defensive code. Harmless, but it implies a state transition that cannot
happen and is misleading to read.

### D6 — `wordWrap` measures bytes, not runes

`internal/ui/help/help.go:123`

Word widths come from `len(word)`, which counts bytes. Accented text therefore
wraps earlier than its rendered width requires: two 5-rune words occupy 11
columns but 21 bytes, so a width of 12 splits them apart.

Low impact today — Rule 129 keeps help content in English US — but it is the same
byte-vs-rune class as [D1](#d1--reportmodalview-emits-invalid-utf-8). Unlike
[D3](#d3--wrapinputlines-loops-forever-when-wrapwidth--0), `wordWrap` does guard
a non-positive width, and that guard is covered by a test so it does not get
"tidied" away.

Pinned by `TestWordWrapMeasuresBytesNotRunes`.

**Fix:** measure with `utf8.RuneCountInString`, or `runewidth.StringWidth` if
double-width glyphs ever appear.

`internal/oci/oci.go:262`

Extraction strips leading `./` and `/` but does not reject `..`, so an archive
member named `../../etc/passwd` survives as a map key containing parent
references.

**Not exploitable today.** The sole consumer, `applyTemplate` in
`internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/model.go:1053`, turns the map into GitLab commit
actions rather than writing to disk, and the server validates the paths.

Recorded because the hazard is latent: any future caller that writes these keys
under a target directory inherits a Zip Slip. Pinned by
`TestExtractTarGzPreservesParentTraversalInKeys`.

**Fix:** reject entries whose cleaned path escapes the root, before returning
them.

---

## 2. Technical debt

### Test coverage

Currently **13.6 %** overall; the agreed target is 80 %, which needs roughly
**+7 700 covered statements** over today's ~1 570.

Phased plan, with the harness and most of phase 1 delivered:

| Phase | Scope | Status |
|---|---|---|

| 1 | Leaf components and pure helpers | **mostly done** — see the table below; `credentials`, `gitlab` and the `ui/theme` complement remain (~255 stmts) |

| 3 | Large views (`workspaces`, `explorer`, `security`, `netdiag`) | pending (~2 470 stmts) |
| 4 | `ui/oci_resources` | pending (~1 995 stmts) |
| 5 | Router and I/O seams (`app`, `scan`, `docker`) | pending (~1 360 stmts) |
| 6 | Remainder to reach 80 % | pending (~400 stmts) |

| Package | Before | Now |

| `internal/ui/shortcut` | 0 % | **100 %** |

## 3. Planned features

Carried over from `todo.md`.

### 3.1 Network diagnostics

- **Port-forwarding manager** — an interactive dashboard to manage port
  redirections to the host machine.

### 3.2 Interactive security remediation

- **Auto-patch assistance** — after a Trivy scan, offer to generate a patch or an
  updated `Dockerfile` that bumps the base image version to clear critical CVEs.
- **Local SAST** — wire security linters (Gitleaks for secrets, IaC linters)
  directly into the Workspace view.

- **Cache-miss analysis** — explain why a build's cache was invalidated, e.g.

### 3.4 Spontaneous dev containers

- **Configuration injection** — inject the developer's dotfiles (vim, zsh,
  aliases) when opening a terminal inside a container.
- **Hot volume mount** — mount the current working directory into a running
  container on the fly, to test a local script without rebuilding the image.

### 3.5 Resource dashboard (embedded mini-htop)

- **TUI charts** — braille-character charts showing live CPU, RAM and network I/O
  for every container in the selected project.
- **Visual alerts** — user-defined thresholds (e.g. memory saturation).

---

## 4. Existing plans

Detailed plans live in `.claude/plans/`. One is referenced directly from the old
`todo.md` and is still outstanding:

- [`platform_compatibility_improvements.md`](../.claude/plans/platform_compatibility_improvements.md)
  — Docker-layer platform portability.

Fixes the byte-vs-rune defect lot from `docs/backlog.md` — **D1**, **D3** and **D6** — plus a fourth site the backlog did not record.

## The defects

**D1** — `ReportModal.View()` truncated long entries with `item[len(item)-52:]`, slicing bytes. Any non-ASCII repository path could put that offset inside a codepoint, after which the whole modal rendered as replacement characters.

**D6** — `help.wordWrap` took word widths from `len(word)`, so accented text wrapped a rune early: two 5-column words measure 21 bytes and split at width 12.

**D3** — `wrapInputLines` looped forever on a non-positive wrap width. The break point collapsed onto `start`, an empty line was appended and `start` never advanced, so the slice grew until the process died. Not reachable today (Rule 133 fixes every caller at 60/80/100).

**Fourth site, unrecorded** — `truncate()` in `internal/ui/security/model.go` sliced bytes exactly like D1, and rendered Trivy finding titles, which are arbitrary upstream text.

## Approach

D1, D6 and the fourth site are one defect in three places, so the logic moved into a shared helper rather than being patched three times (Rule 117). `internal/ui/theme/text.go` exports:

| Helper | Use |
|---|---|
| `StringWidth` | column measurement, replaces `len()` on display values |
| `TruncateWidth` | keeps the head — titles, messages |
| `TruncateTailWidth` | keeps the tail — paths, where trailing segments identify the item |

All three measure **terminal columns**, not runes, so a CJK glyph counts as the 2 columns it occupies. `TruncateTailWidth` stops before a glyph that would overflow rather than splitting it.

`TruncateWidth` needed a guard of its own: `runewidth.Truncate` never shortens its tail marker, so a budget below 3 columns came back wider than requested. That was caught by asserting the column budget across the whole table rather than only the golden strings.

D3's guard refuses to wrap rather than inventing a fallback width — no caller passes a non-positive width, so a silent default would hide a bug rather than surface it.

- `truncateResultLine` in `oci_resources/connectivity_form.go` was deliberately left alone — it counts runes, so it is correct, merely imprecise on double-width glyphs. Folding it in is a cleanup, not a defect fix.
- `go-runewidth` was already in the module graph via bubbles; `go mod tidy` promoted it to direct.

- [x] The two pinned tests that `t.Skip()`d are now real assertions: `TestReportModalViewKeepsMultibyteRunesIntact`, `TestWordWrapMeasuresColumnsNotBytes`
- [x] New table tests for all three helpers, including the column-budget invariant and a double-width-glyph case

# DevDesk Backlog

**Last Updated:** 2026-08-01

Open work for DevDesk: known defects, technical debt, and planned features.
Replaces the former `todo.md` at the repository root. Items completed there
(network topology visualisation, inter-container ping/curl) have been dropped
rather than carried over.

---

## 1. Known defects

None of these are fixed. Each is reachable from the current code unless noted.

### D1 — `ReportModal.View()` emits invalid UTF-8

`internal/ui/components/report_modal.go:136-139`

Long entries are truncated with `item[len(item)-52:]`, which slices **bytes**, not
runes. When the resulting offset falls inside a multi-byte codepoint the rendered
output is no longer valid UTF-8 and the terminal shows replacement characters.

Reachable with any non-ASCII repository path. Pinned by
`TestReportModalViewTruncationSplitsMultibyteRunes`, which `t.Skip()`s with
instructions once the truncation becomes rune-aware.

**Fix:** truncate on `[]rune`, and measure width with `runewidth` rather than
`len()`.

### D2 — The "permanent delete" checkbox is documented as locked but is not

`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:35` and `:99-105`

`NewDeleteConfirmModalPermanent` pre-checks *Immediate deletion* and its doc
comment states the box is non-modifiable ("pré-cochée et non modifiable"). Nothing
enforces that: `space` and `enter` on the checkbox still toggle it.

A project already marked for deletion can therefore be sent through a
grace-period delete that the caller does not expect. Pinned by
`TestDeleteConfirmModalPermanentCheckboxIsStillToggleable`.

**Fix:** carry a `locked` flag on the modal and make the toggle a no-op when set,
or drop the claim from the doc comment.

### D3 — `wrapInputLines` loops forever when `wrapWidth <= 0`

`internal/ui/components/wrapped_input.go:135`

With a non-positive wrap width the loop makes no progress: `breakAt` collapses to
`start`, an empty line is appended, and `start` never advances — the line slice
grows until the process runs out of memory.

**Not reachable today.** Every caller passes 60, 80 or 100 per Rule 133. Latent
only, which is why no test covers it (the test would hang).

**Fix:** guard the entry point — return a single line when `wrapWidth < 1`.

### D4 — `DeleteConfirmModal` uses `Tab` for field navigation

`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:89-97`

`tab` / `shift+tab` cycle checkbox → Yes → No. Rule 135 reserves those keys for
tab switching and assigns field navigation to `↑ / ↓` exclusively.

Cosmetic in isolation, but it is the kind of inconsistency Rule 135 exists to
prevent. Changing it alters muscle memory, so it needs a deliberate call rather
than a drive-by fix.

### D5 — Unreachable focus clamp in `CreationForm`

`internal/ui/components/creation_form.go:221-223`

After cycling the resource type, the code clamps `focusedField` down to
`maxField()`. The surrounding branch only runs when `focusedField == 0`, and
`maxField()` is never below 4, so the clamp can never fire.

Dead defensive code. Harmless, but it implies a state transition that cannot
happen and is misleading to read.

### D6 — `wordWrap` measures bytes, not runes

`internal/ui/help/help.go:123`

Word widths come from `len(word)`, which counts bytes. Accented text therefore
wraps earlier than its rendered width requires: two 5-rune words occupy 11
columns but 21 bytes, so a width of 12 splits them apart.

Low impact today — Rule 129 keeps help content in English US — but it is the same
byte-vs-rune class as [D1](#d1--reportmodalview-emits-invalid-utf-8). Unlike
[D3](#d3--wrapinputlines-loops-forever-when-wrapwidth--0), `wordWrap` does guard
a non-positive width, and that guard is covered by a test so it does not get
"tidied" away.

Pinned by `TestWordWrapMeasuresBytesNotRunes`.

**Fix:** measure with `utf8.RuneCountInString`, or `runewidth.StringWidth` if
double-width glyphs ever appear.

### D7 — `extractTarGz` keeps parent references in archive paths

`internal/oci/oci.go:262`

Extraction strips leading `./` and `/` but does not reject `..`, so an archive
member named `../../etc/passwd` survives as a map key containing parent
references.

**Not exploitable today.** The sole consumer, `applyTemplate` in
`internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/model.go:1053`, turns the map into GitLab commit
actions rather than writing to disk, and the server validates the paths.

Recorded because the hazard is latent: any future caller that writes these keys
under a target directory inherits a Zip Slip. Pinned by
`TestExtractTarGzPreservesParentTraversalInKeys`.

**Fix:** reject entries whose cleaned path escapes the root, before returning
them.

---

## 2. Technical debt

### Test coverage

Currently **13.6 %** overall; the agreed target is 80 %, which needs roughly
**+7 700 covered statements** over today's ~1 570.

Phased plan, with the harness and most of phase 1 delivered:

| Phase | Scope | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `internal/ui/testutil` Bubble Tea harness | **done** (100 %) |
| 1 | Leaf components and pure helpers | **mostly done** — see the table below; `credentials`, `gitlab` and the `ui/theme` complement remain (~255 stmts) |
| 2 | Mid-size view state machines (`status`, `containers`, `dashboard`, `gitlab/auth`) | pending (~1 240 stmts) |
| 3 | Large views (`workspaces`, `explorer`, `security`, `netdiag`) | pending (~2 470 stmts) |
| 4 | `ui/oci_resources` | pending (~1 995 stmts) |
| 5 | Router and I/O seams (`app`, `scan`, `docker`) | pending (~1 360 stmts) |
| 6 | Remainder to reach 80 % | pending (~400 stmts) |

Phase 1 progress:

| Package | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/ui/testutil` | — | **100 %** (new) |
| `internal/ui/shortcut` | 0 % | **100 %** |
| `internal/ui/help` | 0 % | **96.7 %** |
| `internal/ui/components` | 0 % | **79.8 %** |
| `internal/oci` | 0 % | **33.6 %** |
| `internal/credentials` | 29.5 % | unchanged |
| `internal/gitlab` | 7.5 % | unchanged |

`internal/oci` stops at 33.6 % because the remaining statements are registry HTTP
paths (`DownloadTemplate`, `listCatalog`, `ListTemplates`) that need a fuller
`httptest` fixture — a manifest plus a gzipped layer — rather than the
single-response stubs used so far.

Phase 5 requires a refactor before it can start: `internal/docker/client.go`
shells out to the Docker CLI directly, so it needs an injectable execution seam
to be testable.

### Files over the 800-line ceiling

The project's own coding rules cap files at 800 lines. Eight exceed it:

| File | Lines |
|---|---|
| `internal/ui/security/model.go` | 1785 |
| `internal/ui/oci_resources/update.go` | 1556 |
| `internal/app/app.go` | 1333 |
| `internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/model.go` | 1214 |
| `internal/ui/workspaces/model.go` | 1133 |
| `internal/docker/client.go` | 1069 |
| `internal/ui/netdiag/model.go` | 995 |
| `internal/ui/oci_resources/registry_browser.go` | 822 |

This interacts with the coverage work: writing several thousand statements of
tests against these files before splitting them freezes their current structure.
Decide the order deliberately.

### Race detector cannot run locally

`mise run test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler on `PATH`. Without one
it fails with `cgo: C compiler "gcc" not found`. Bubble Tea `Cmd`s run
concurrently, so this is the check most likely to catch a Rule 110 violation —
it should run in CI even if local machines lack a toolchain.

---

## 3. Planned features

Carried over from `todo.md`.

### 3.1 Network diagnostics

- **Port-forwarding manager** — an interactive dashboard to manage port
  redirections to the host machine.

### 3.2 Interactive security remediation

- **Auto-patch assistance** — after a Trivy scan, offer to generate a patch or an
  updated `Dockerfile` that bumps the base image version to clear critical CVEs.
- **Local SAST** — wire security linters (Gitleaks for secrets, IaC linters)
  directly into the Workspace view.

### 3.3 OCI build and cache analyser

- **Layer visualisation** — analyse a local image and show the size of each
  layer, in the spirit of `dive`. Intended approach:
  - Integrated via `google/go-containerregistry` ("daemonless", no dependency on
    the Docker daemon).
  - Talk to OCI registries directly, pulling manifests and configs without
    downloading the whole image.
  - Stream layers in memory (`tar`) to rebuild the filesystem tree.
  - Compute wasted space by detecting whiteout files (`.wh.`).
- **Cache-miss analysis** — explain why a build's cache was invalidated, e.g.
  "`package.json` changed, invalidating the cache".

### 3.4 Spontaneous dev containers

- **Configuration injection** — inject the developer's dotfiles (vim, zsh,
  aliases) when opening a terminal inside a container.
- **Hot volume mount** — mount the current working directory into a running
  container on the fly, to test a local script without rebuilding the image.

### 3.5 Resource dashboard (embedded mini-htop)

- **TUI charts** — braille-character charts showing live CPU, RAM and network I/O
  for every container in the selected project.
- **Visual alerts** — user-defined thresholds (e.g. memory saturation).

---

## 4. Existing plans

Detailed plans live in `.claude/plans/`. One is referenced directly from the old
`todo.md` and is still outstanding:

- [`platform_compatibility_improvements.md`](../.claude/plans/platform_compatibility_improvements.md)
  — Docker-layer platform portability.
